Employee cost rose 29% on a 35% Haryana minimum wage increase from 1 April 2026.

US tariffs currently 10%; exports to the US only USD 3.5-4 million this year.

penalties.authority: Office of Divisional Commissioner, Government of the NCT of Delhi, Revenue Department: Stamp & Registration Branch, through the Collector of Stamps
penalties.details: Proceedings were initiated by the Authority under the provisions of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 as applicable to the National Capital Territory of Delhi for determination of stamp duty payable in relation to issuance/allotment of certain shares by the Company. In this regard, the Company received two Show Cause Notices dated February 18, 2026 and March 17, 2026 from the Authority in relation to the allotment of shares made on November 1, 2021 and August 4, 2022, respectively. The Company responded to the Show Cause Notices and, inter-alia, contended that it had duly discharged the applicable stamp duty in respect of the subject share allotments and that the proceedings initiated by the Authority under Article 19 of Schedule IA to the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 (as applicable to the NCT of Delhi) were not maintainable in view of Sections 9A(2) and 9A(3) of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899. Pursuant to the proceedings, an order dated June 15, 2026 has been passed by the Authority adjudging the Company liable to pay alleged deficit stamp duty of Rs. 1,00,25,820/- (Rupees One crore twenty-five thousand eight hundred and twenty only) along with penalty of Rs. 1,50,00,000/- (Rupees One crore fifty Lakh only). Pertinently, the Show Cause Notices issued to the Company pertain only to the allotment of shares on November 1, 2021 and August 4, 2022. However, the Order proceeds to determine and levy alleged deficit stamp duty and penalty in relation to share allotments purportedly made on August 2, 2022, January 31, 2024, March 8, 2024 and August 5, 2024. The Company is taking appropriate legal advice to defend the matter, as it believes that it has good grounds to challenge and contest the demand raised by the authorities. Accordingly, the Company is in the process of pursuing appropriate legal remedies challenging the Order.

operating_notes.text: About 450 dialysis machines placed in FY26 took the installed base to roughly 1,000 machines, with about 20% more machine sales planned in FY27.
Citieffe and PendraCare contributed ₹65 Cr of Q4FY26 revenue, about ₹43-44 Cr from Citieffe, and currently run at 12-14% EBITDA margin against a 18-20% target in 2-3 years.
Capacity utilisation after QIP-1 is about 65-70%, and the group holds close to 399 patents.
Cash conversion cycle was 140 days in Q1FY27, same as March.
Stand-alone working capital debt is about ₹250 Cr revolving credit; Citieffe loan is EUR 9 million with EUR 1.5-2 million annual repayment.
Company has 399 patents and exports to 125 countries.
